chunks: From him (Al-Shaykh) from Ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil ibn Dirraj from Zurarah who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man is given goods, and it is said to him, 'What you have added/excessed on such and such (price) is for you.' He said, 'There is no harm (it is permissible).'

key_terms.اِزْدَدْتَ: You have added/excessed (referring to profit or added value)
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no harm / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to keep the excess profit when given goods with a specified base price in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the permissibility of a specific commercial arrangement where a buyer provides goods with an agreement to retain any surplus value or profit above a base price, a practice known as *al-ziyadah*. Imam al-Sadiq’s (peace be upon him) concise ruling of 'la ba'sa' (no harm) underscores the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding contractual terms, provided there is no ambiguity (*gharar*) or exploitation. This ruling is frequently cited by scholars to validate flexible pricing models and profit-sharing agreements in trade.
